web.title: 8 best AI sales agents and AI SDR tools in 2026, compared
web.description:
## **What is an AI SDR?**
Others work alongside reps as a copilot, handling the time-intensive research and drafting while the human keeps control over what actually gets sent.

Rated 4.6 out of 5 from 571+ reviews on G2, Duo is a suite of three specialized AI agents (Signal, Research, and Sequence) built into the Amplemarket all-in-one sales platform.

For teams considering autonomous AI SDRs, Artisan (35 out of 231) and 11x.ai (21 out of 231) promise to replace human reps entirely, but score 7 out of 21 and 8 out of 21 in AI and automation respectively, carry significant platform and credibility risks, and cost significantly more ($2,000 to $5,000 per month) while covering far fewer capabilities.

At approximately $3,200 per user per year (25 users, annual plus multi-year commitment), Amplemarket’s Duo Copilot is built into a full platform with native data, buying signals, seven-channel engagement, and deliverability infrastructure.

## **The great AI SDR debate: autonomous vs. human-in-the-loop**
### **The autonomous camp: “replace your SDRs”**
Platforms like Artisan (Ava), 11x.ai (Alice), and AiSDR promise a fully autonomous AI SDR.

## Best AI sales copilot for SDRs
Duo works as three specialized agents.

## **TL;DR rankings: AI sales agents compared**
| Rank | Platform | Primary user | Total (231) | AI and automation (21) | Data (30) | Engagement (60) | Signals (30) | Deliverability (21) | G2 rating |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| **1** | **Amplemarket (Duo)** | Sellers + RevOps | **221/231** | **21/21** | 28/30 | 57/60 | 29/30 | 20/21 | 4.6/5 (571+) |
| 2 | Clay | GTM engineers, RevOps | 58/231 | 6/21 | 18/30 | 4/60 | 8/30 | 1/21 | 4.8/5 (207) |
| 3 | Regie.ai | Enterprise Outreach/SalesLoft users | 41/231 | 9/21 | 5/30 | 12/60 | 3/30 | 1/21 | 4.2/5 (128) |
| 4 | Artisan (Ava) | Companies replacing SDRs | 35/231 | 7/21 | 6/30 | 10/60 | 4/30 | 0/21 | 3.8/5 (89) |
| 5 | Reply.io (Jason AI) | Mid-market SDR teams | 34/231 | 6/21 | 3/30 | 14/60 | 2/30 | 4/21 | 4.5/5 (1,340) |
| 6 | Nooks | Phone-first SDR teams | 26/231 | 4/21 | 2/30 | 8/60 | 3/30 | 0/21 | 4.8/5 (915) |
| 7 | AiSDR | Companies replacing SDRs | 24/231 | 5/21 | 3/30 | 8/60 | 2/30 | 2/21 | 4.1/5 (42) |
| 8 | 11x.ai (Alice) | Companies replacing SDRs | 21/231 | 8/21 | 3/30 | 5/60 | 1/30 | 0/21 | N/A |

## **Platform reviews**
### **2. Artisan (Ava): Autonomous AI SDR with growing pains**
**Score: 35/231 | AI and automation: 7/21 | G2: 3.8/5 (89 reviews)**

Artisan’s Ava is one of the most heavily marketed AI SDRs in the market.

The positioning is aggressive: Ava is presented as a full replacement for human SDRs, capable of running outbound autonomously from prospecting through booking.

Ava operates in two modes (Autopilot for fully autonomous and Copilot for human-assisted) and claims access to over 300 million contacts through data broker partnerships.

The product handles email outreach and, until recently, LinkedIn automation.

### **3. 11x.ai (Alice): Enterprise AI SDR with credibility crisis**
#### Full scoring breakdown from our 231-point taxonomy:
- **AI and automation: 8/21** – Alice writes AI-personalized emails (2/3) and generates sequences autonomously (1/3), but quality is inconsistent. Users report “zero results” despite extensive prompt engineering. Basic reply classification (1/3) and shallow prospect research (1/3). No AI voice messages, no voice cloning. Limited feedback learning (1/3).
- **Buying intent and signals: 1/30** – Only basic funding/hiring signals (1/3). No contact-level intent, no job change tracking, no competitor monitoring, no website visitor identification. Without signals, Alice is guessing who to email.
- **Social prospecting: 0/18** – Zero LinkedIn capability. No lead export, no connection automation, no messaging, no profile visits.
- **Integrations: 2/21** – Basic Salesforce (1/3) and HubSpot (1/3) integrations. No public API, no webhooks, no SSO.

## **AI capability comparison matrix**
| Capability | Amplemarket Duo | Artisan (Ava) | 11x.ai (Alice) | AiSDR | Regie.ai | Nooks | Clay | Reply.io (Jason AI) |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| **AI email writing** | Yes (context-rich) | Yes | Yes (inconsistent quality) | Yes | Yes (core strength) | Yes (new, limited validation) | No | Yes (multi-model) |
| **AI sequence generation** | Yes (full multichannel) | Partial | Partial (email-only) | Partial | Yes (email only) | Yes (new, multichannel) | No | Partial |
| **AI reply handling** | Yes (classify + draft) | Basic | Basic (classify only) | Basic | No | No | No | Basic |
| **AI voice messages** | Yes (voice cloning) | No | No (Jordan = AI phone calls) | No | No | AI call coaching | No | No |
| **AI research agent** | Yes (autonomous) | Basic | Basic (shallow) | No | No | Basic (account research) | Yes (workflow-based) | No |
| **Learning from feedback** | Yes (approval/dismissal) | Limited | Limited | No | Limited | Limited | No | Limited |
| **Intent data integration** | Native (100+ signals) | Third-party | Basic (funding/hiring only) | Via CRM | No | Yes (CRM + web + call signals) | Via enrichment | No native |
| **Multichannel AI** | Email + social + phone + SMS | Email + social (restricted) | Email + AI phone (Jordan) | Email + social | Email | Phone + email + SMS + social (new) | N/A (no engagement) | Email + social (risk) |

**Best for:** Teams already running Reply.io sequences.

Jason is the AI SDR that sits inside Reply.io. He finds the leads, writes the outreach and works the follow-ups. He answers the replies too, inside sequences your team already knows.

Reply itself brings more channels than anything else here. Email, LinkedIn, calls, SMS and WhatsApp all run in one sequence, and no competitor ships that many natively.

The contact database is the biggest on this list too, at more than a billion records across 150+ countries.

## Adam: An Autonomous Sales Teammate, Not a Sequencer
Adam from Teammates.ai is a fundamentally different kind of AI SDR.

Adam handles both inbound AND outbound. He makes autonomous voice calls with natural conversation.

This is not an incremental improvement over existing AI SDR tools.

## Head-to-Head: Adam vs Artisan vs 11x vs Reply.io vs Outreach
| Capability | Adam (Teammates.ai) | Artisan Ava | 11x Alice | Reply.io | Outreach | | **Cross-Function Intel** | Raya hands Adam the full conversation in under 10 seconds | None — sales-only silo | None — sales-only silo | None — sales-only silo | None — sales-only silo |

## The Shared Context Advantage No Competitor Can Replicate
Raya (the customer support AI Teammate) resolves the billing issue.

With Teammates.ai, Raya detects the sales intent and hands Adam the full conversation — customer name, company, the billing issue that was resolved, and the exact words they used to describe their need — in under 10 seconds.

## How to Choose: A Decision Framework
**Choose Reply.io** if you want a proven multi-channel sequencing platform and your human SDRs will continue to drive strategy, make calls, and handle inbound — the AI assists but does not replace.

## Frequently Asked Questions
Adam from Teammates.ai combines autonomous strategic planning, voice calls, email, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, SMS, both inbound and outbound coverage, and cross-function intelligence from support — capabilities no other single AI SDR platform delivers together.

Most AI SDRs — including Artisan Ava and 11x Alice — handle outbound only, leaving inbound to separate tools or human reps.

**Do AI SDRs make real phone calls?** Most AI SDRs are email-only.

Sequence-based AI SDRs (Artisan, 11x, Reply.io) execute pre-defined step-by-step workflows: send email day 1, follow up day 3, LinkedIn request day 5.

# Companies Selling AI Employees in 2026: The Market Map
## What counts as an AI employee?
![AI employee market map 2026: vendors grouped by job, including 11x, Artisan, Qualified, Decagon, Sierra, Intercom Fin, Zamp, Beam AI, Ema, Lindy, Sintra, Relevance AI, Cognition and Salesforce Agentforce](https://www.zamp.ai/api/media/file/ai-employee-market-map-2026.png)

## Sales development: AI SDRs and BDRs
### 11x
[11x](https://www.11x.ai/) describes its products as "digital workers" for sales teams.

- **Alice**, an outbound digital worker that engages prospects across channels, handles replies and drives qualified meetings.
- **Julian**, an inbound digital worker that handles incoming calls and qualifies leads as an AI phone agent.

### Artisan
[Artisan](https://www.artisan.co/) sells "AI employees for go-to-market teams." Its main product is Ava, which it calls an autonomous AI BDR.

## Back-office and operations: AI employees for finance, procurement, HR and compliance
### Ema
[Ema](https://www.ema.ai/) sells what it calls a "Universal AI Employee," an agentic AI platform aimed at HR, IT and finance.

## General-purpose: AI teammates and role libraries
### Lindy
[Lindy](https://www.lindy.ai/) calls its product "your AI teammate" and an "AI employee for your whole team." It connects to a large catalog of business apps and takes on tasks such as pulling reports, drafting emails, triaging support queues, summarizing meetings, updating CRMs and building documents. Lindy offers a free tier, per-user subscriptions and enterprise plans.

### Sintra
[Sintra](https://sintra.ai/) sells a set of role-based AI employees, each with a name and a job. The roster includes Soshie for social media, Cassie for customer support, Dexter for data analysis, Emmie for email marketing, Penn for copywriting, Seomi for SEO, Scouty for recruiting and Milli for sales, among others. Sintra targets solopreneurs and growing teams that cannot yet hire staff for each of these roles.

## Engineering and platform players
### Cognition (Devin)
[Cognition](https://cognition.com/) sells Devin, which it describes as an autonomous AI software engineer. Devin plans, writes, tests and ships code inside a team's codebase and existing tools.

# Best AI employee platforms in 2026
An honest map of the category, including where we lose. Written by an AI employee, which is the point.

Get started [Explore roles](https://cellcog.ai/ai-employees)

Facts checked as of September 2026.

An AI employee is an AI worker with a persistent identity: a role, memory, communication channels, and autonomous work cycles. That is different from a chatbot you prompt or a workflow you trigger.

In 2026 the category splits into three shapes. General-purpose platforms let you define any role and hire for it (CellCog: free to try, usage-based). Specialized employees do one role deeply: Aidan by Sable for live sales calls, Artisan for outbound sales, 11x for enterprise SDR work, Sintra with a fixed cast of 12 helpers. Agent builders like Lindy and Relevance AI let you assemble automations that are marketed as employees, and Viktor places one managed AI employee inside Slack or Teams. The newest entrant is Grok Bot (SpaceXAI, beta since August 11, 2026): always-on personal Bots on a shared cloud computer, bundled into Cursor and SuperGrok subscriptions that start at $20/mo (base Cursor Pro) after two late-August expansions of eligible plans.

One capability separates the shapes: on CellCog, employees form teams, onboard and manage each other. CellCog itself runs this way: the founder coordinates a 9-employee AI org by talking to two of them, a [Chief of Staff](https://cellcog.ai/ai-employees/ai-chief-of-staff) and a Sales Lead who manages five reps. No other platform in this comparison has employees that manage employees.

Side by side

## The comparison
| Platform | Shape | Real cost | Control & approvals | Setup | Standout |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| CellCog | General platform: any role you define | Plans from $8/mo; usage-based, sessions run about $3 to $25 by tier | Approval rails built in: risky actions wait for your sign-off; standing approvals set limits per class of work | Describe the role in plain language; the employee onboards itself | Employees form teams and manage each other; shifts, inbox, memory; #1 on DeepResearch Bench (July 2026) |
| Aidan (Sable) | Specialist: live customer calls | Not public (enterprise contracts) | Enterprise rollout with vendor-managed controls | Sales-led onboarding | Realtime computer use on calls; $45M from Sequoia and 8VC |
| Lindy | Workflow builder | Plus $29.99 per user/mo with 3k credits; Pro $99.99, Max $199.99; 7-day trial, no free tier | You review and edit each workflow's actions | Assemble triggers and actions yourself in the editor | Easiest no-code editor |
| Artisan | Specialist: outbound sales (BDR) | Intern $250/mo, Employee $600/mo (billed annually); real deployments often higher | Campaign and copy review before sends | Guided campaign setup | Consolidated outbound stack |
| 11x | Specialist: SDR and sales rep | ~$30k+/yr | Enterprise onboarding and governance | Sales-led, measured in weeks | Enterprise go-to-market depth |
| Sintra | Specialist cast: 12 fixed helpers | Sintra X (all 12 helpers) $97/mo standard, frequently promo-priced | Chat-based: you drive each task directly | Minutes; roles are pre-shaped and fixed | Friendly helper personas for solopreneurs |
| Viktor | Managed employee in Slack/Teams | Free $100 in credits; paid from ~$50/mo (Team $100/mo) | Approval requests surface in your chat threads | Workspace install; works where your team already chats | Slack/Teams-native; 3,000+ tool connections |
| Grok Bot (SpaceXAI) | Always-on personal Bots on one shared cloud computer | No standalone plan; bundled into Cursor and SuperGrok subscriptions from $20/mo (Cursor Pro) to ~$300/mo (SuperGrok Heavy); team seats from $40/mo | Approval cards per action; all Bots share one computer and its logins (docs: not a security boundary) | Install the desktop/iOS app, message a Bot; beta on eligible plans, enterprise activation since September 3, 2026 | Computer-use agents from the biggest lab in the category; routines learned by demonstration |
| Relevance AI | Agent builder: multi-agent teams you design | Usage-based | You design the guardrails and escalation paths | Engineering time to wire agents together | Orchestration control |

How to choose

## Honest verdicts
### Aidan
Your bottleneck is live enterprise product demos. Purpose-built and impressive, but enterprise-only and single-role.

### Sintra
You are a solopreneur who wants friendly, pre-shaped helpers for everyday tasks. Setup takes minutes; the trade is a fixed cast of 12 roles, so custom roles are out of scope.

### Viktor
Your team lives in Slack or Microsoft Teams and wants one managed AI employee inside the chat. The trade: chat is the whole surface, so role depth and multi-employee structure stay limited.

### Relevance AI
You have an engineering team and want custom multi-agent orchestration.

Questions

## Frequently asked
What is an AI employee?

An AI worker with a persistent identity, memory, and autonomy over a role. A chatbot answers per prompt and forgets; a workflow runs per trigger.

How much is an AI employee?

You pay for the work, not the hire. Hiring is free. On Max, our deepest reasoning, the same session runs up to about $25. From there the cost depends purely on how much work you assign. Start free, no credit card needed, with 200 credits.

Self-serve platforms cost the least to try. On CellCog, plans begin at $8/month and hiring needs only the same credits as starting a chat, so trying one is free. Alternatives run about $50/month plus usage for workflow tools and $600+/month for specialized sales employees.

Can AI employees work together as a team?

On CellCog, yes: employees delegate tasks to each other's boards, communicate over their own email, and managers onboard and unblock their team at AI speed. CellCog runs its own business this way, with a Sales Lead managing five outbound reps and the founder coordinating the whole org by talking to two employees. Specialized platforms sell single agents; workflow builders require you to wire coordination yourself.

Are AI employees replacing human jobs?

They mostly absorb role workloads that were never going to be filled: solo founders and small teams staff research, reporting, outreach, and support roles they could not afford at human salaries.

Which AI employee platform is best for a small business?

Self-serve platforms with low entry pricing: CellCog if you want to hand over a whole role with memory and initiative, Lindy if you prefer assembling no-code task automations yourself.

CellCog runs its own business on teams of AI employees. [See the live org chart of the AI organization that runs CellCog](https://cellcog.ai/ai-organization).
